name: review_story_lock_guard
summary: Wrap review_story in _plan_lock so a concurrent call can't race the scheduler's own internal review and clobber an already-merged story's status
agent_instructions:
ROOT CAUSE (already diagnosed live, do not re-investigate): `review_story` (`pipeline/server.py`, decorated `@mcp.tool()`, defined ~line 1922) is the ONLY story-mutating MCP tool in this file that does NOT acquire `_plan_lock`. Every sibling that reads-then-writes a story's manifest entry already does: `patch_story` (~line 1738: `with _plan_lock(plan_name) as acquired: if not acquired: return {"ok": True, "skipped": "locked", "reason": "another dispatch/ingest/interrupt is in progress for this plan"}`), `set_story_status` (same pattern, ~line 1773), `dispatch_story`, `interrupt_story`, and `advance_pipeline`/`_advance_pipeline_locked` itself (~line 2281). `_plan_lock` (`pipeline/concurrency.py`) is an `fcntl`-based, cross-process, per-plan-name flock, reentrant per-thread (so `_advance_pipeline_locked`'s own internal call to `review_story` at ~line 2492, made while it ALREADY holds the lock for the whole tick, will continue to work exactly as it does today - reentrant acquisition inside the same thread is instant, not a deadlock).

Because `review_story` itself never tries to acquire this lock, a call to it that does NOT originate from inside an already-locked `_advance_pipeline_locked` tick (e.g. a manual/interactive `mcp__pipeline__review_story` call, or two overlapping scheduler processes) can run fully concurrently with a tick's own internal review+merge sequence. This is exactly what happened live on 2026-07-21 (Mode 29, see project memory `project_dispatch_failure_modes.md` MODE 29 and `retros/tdd-split-unconditional-and-review-race_2026-07-21.md`): a manual `review_story` call and the scheduler's own tick both read the same story while it still said `tests_passed`; the tick's own path won the race, reviewed, opened a PR, and merged (worktree cleaned up, status -> `done`) - but the OTHER, now-stale call was still in flight and, on completing, found a (correctly) nonexistent worktree, reported `REQUEST_CHANGES`, and overwrote the manifest's status for the already-`done`, already-merged story back to `changes_requested`. Nothing on GitHub was ever wrong, but the manifest lied, and a subsequent `approve_merge` failed on the stale precondition, requiring a manual `gh pr view`/`git log origin/master` cross-check to prove the manifest wrong.

**NOTE - do not confuse this with an already-fixed, different guard**: `review_story` already has an EARLY-EXIT check for a story whose status is anything other than `tests_passed` AT THE MOMENT IT'S CALLED (see the existing `if story.get("status") != "tests_passed": ... return {"ok": True, "status": ..., "skipped": "not_reviewable_state"}` near the top of the function, and its full test coverage in `test_review_story_stale_guard.py` - read-only, do NOT modify, do not re-implement, do not re-derive its logic). That guard correctly handles SEQUENTIAL staleness (a call that arrives after the status has ALREADY changed). It does NOT and CANNOT handle the Mode 29 race, because the race is about two calls whose manifest reads happen to interleave BEFORE either one writes - both calls can pass that entry check seeing `tests_passed`, since neither has written yet. Only serializing the two calls (the lock) closes that window. Do not touch the existing entry-status guard's code or tests; your fix is purely adding lock acquisition around the function.

FIX (single, contained change): wrap the ENTIRE body of `review_story` (everything currently between its `_validate_key` calls at the top and its final return) in `with _plan_lock(plan_name) as acquired:`, mirroring `patch_story`'s exact pattern (read that function first, ~line 1717-1751, as your template - same import, same skip-return shape). If `not acquired`, return immediately: `{"ok": True, "skipped": "locked", "reason": "another dispatch/ingest/interrupt/review is in progress for this plan"}` (reuse the exact wording style of the sibling functions' reason strings - list "review" alongside the others since this is now one of the operations the lock covers). `_plan_lock` is already imported into `pipeline/server.py` (used by other functions in the same file) - do not add a new import, just use the existing name. Do NOT change anything about what happens INSIDE the lock - the entire existing function body (the entry guard, the SHA guard, the reviewer dispatch, verdict handling, PR opening, rework/park logic) stays exactly as it is today, just now wrapped.

TDD: write the tests FIRST and confirm them failing before writing the fix. Create a NEW test file `test_review_story_lock_guard.py` (this repo's established one-file-per-guard convention - see `test_review_story_same_sha.py`, `test_review_story_stale_guard.py` as siblings; read them ONLY for their fixture patterns - the `plan_dir`/`agents_dir` monkeypatch fixtures and the `_write_manifest_with_story`/`_read_story` helpers in `test_review_story_stale_guard.py` - do NOT edit either existing file). For the lock-held simulation, mirror `test_patch_story_skips_when_lock_held` in `test_pipeline_mcp_server.py` (~line 1323) EXACTLY - it opens `plan_dir / "<plan_name>.lock"` with `os.open(..., os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR)`, takes `fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)` to simulate another process holding the lock, calls the function under test inside a `try`, then releases in `finally`. Read-only reference, do not modify that file either.

Required test cases in the new file:
1. `test_review_story_skips_when_lock_held`: with the plan's lock file already held externally (mirroring the pattern above) and a story at `status="tests_passed"`, call `p.review_story(plan_name, story_key)`. Assert: `result["ok"] is True`, `result["skipped"] == "locked"`, `_run_reviewer` is never invoked (monkeypatch it with a sentinel that appends to a list, assert the list stays empty), `_open_pr` is never invoked (same sentinel pattern), and the on-disk manifest bytes are byte-for-byte unchanged from before the call (same `_manifest_bytes`-style comparison `test_review_story_stale_guard.py` already uses - read that file's helper and replicate the same helper function in your new file, don't import across test files).
2. `test_review_story_proceeds_normally_when_lock_is_free`: same `tests_passed` story, NO lock held. Assert `_run_reviewer` IS invoked, an APPROVE verdict flows through to `status == "pr_open"` exactly as the existing (untouched) `test_review_story_tests_passed_still_runs_reviewer` in `test_review_story_stale_guard.py` already verifies - this is your regression check that wrapping the function in the lock didn't change ordinary behavior. Mirror that test's mock shape for `_run_reviewer`/`_open_pr`.
3. `test_review_story_lock_released_after_call`: call `p.review_story` once on a free lock (any status, e.g. `todo` so it hits the early skip fast), then verify the lock is free afterward by taking a NON-blocking `fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)` on the same `<plan_name>.lock` path yourself immediately after and asserting it succeeds (no `BlockingIOError`) - proving `review_story` released the lock (via the `with` statement, not an explicit unlock) even on its early-exit skip path.
4. `test_review_story_internal_call_from_advance_pipeline_still_works`: this is the reentrancy regression check - the whole point of this fix is that `_advance_pipeline_locked`'s existing internal call to `review_story` (already holding the lock for its tick) must keep working unchanged. Don't call `_advance_pipeline_locked` directly (too heavy/unrelated setup); instead, directly simulate the reentrant-call shape: acquire `_plan_lock(plan_name)` yourself in the test (using the real context manager, not the raw `fcntl` file), and INSIDE that `with` block, call `p.review_story(plan_name, story_key)` on a `tests_passed` story. Assert it behaves exactly like case 2 above (reviewer invoked, APPROVE flows through, PR opened) - i.e. `acquired` is still True on the nested acquisition and nothing is skipped as locked. This is the test that would catch an accidental non-reentrant lock choice breaking production's own internal call path.

Testable success criteria: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest test_review_story_lock_guard.py -v` all green (4/4). Then `.venv/bin/python -m pytest --override-ini=testpaths=. --ignore=tests -q` (this repo's full suite) has zero new failures - in particular `test_review_story_same_sha.py`, `test_review_story_stale_guard.py`, and every test in `test_pipeline_mcp_server.py` whose name contains `review_story` or `advance_pipeline` must be untouched and still pass, since this change only adds a lock acquisition around an unchanged function body. `ruff check pipeline/server.py test_review_story_lock_guard.py` clean. Commit your work.
